title: WHAT IS THIS GOD HAS DONE?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "At the place where they stopped for the night one of them opened his sack to get feed for his donkey, and he saw his silver in the mouth of his sack. 'My silver has been returned,' he said to his brothers. 'Here it is in my sack.' Their hearts sank and, trembling, they turned to each other and said, 'What is this that God has done to us?'" - Gen 42:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
On the journey home, one brother opens his sack and finds his silver returned. But instead of rejoicing at this apparent good fortune, "their hearts sank" and they trembled, crying out, "What is this that God has done to us?" A gift meant as kindness fills them not with joy but with fear.

Why would returned money frighten them so? Because their consciences were awakened and guilty. They feared this would look like theft, that they might be accused and punished. A clear conscience would have received the silver as a blessing; but a guilty conscience turned even grace into a threat. Their guilt made them read God's kindness as God's judgment.

This is what unresolved guilt does. It distorts how we see everything, even the good. When we are burdened by sin, we can begin to view God as against us, interpreting His gifts as traps and His mercy as menace. A guilty heart struggles to receive grace, because it is braced for punishment.

Notice, too, that they now sense God at work: "What is this that God has done to us?" Their eyes are beginning to open to His hand in their circumstances — a first step, even if mixed with fear. God was indeed at work, but for their good, not their harm. Do not let guilt make you misread God's heart. When we come clean before Him, we can finally receive His grace as the good gift it truly is.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does unresolved guilt make me misread God's kindness as threat?
2. Am I able to receive God's grace, or am I braced for punishment?
3. Where do I need to come clean so I can see God's heart rightly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, do not let guilt distort how I see You. Free my conscience so I can receive Your grace with joy rather than fear. Help me to see Your hand at work for my good. Amen.
